title: Bistable buckled aluminum-nitride nanobeam as a leak-free bit
idea: Periodic-table walk, Al+N (13,7): a pre-stressed 100 nm AlN beam buckles into one of two stable states; a piezoelectric kick (ns, since resonance is ~GHz) flips it and capacitive sensing reads it; there is no contact, so wear stays at resonator-class (>1e15 cycles) and nothing leaks.
why: No capacitor, no access-transistor leakage tail, no refresh; Al, N and Si only, and no high-k or W.

title: Solderless compression-attach DRAM packages movable between board generations
idea: Worsen: solder LPDDR and DDR chips permanently to boards, so one dead CPU scraps all of its memory. Flip: seat each DRAM package in a spring-pin elastomer socket with a clamp frame (a chip-level CAMM), so packages can be lifted out, retested and re-seated in the next server generation.
why: Raises usable supply by extending DRAM service life 2-3x with no desolder or reball damage: scarce-resource intensity per bit-year falls ~50%.

title: Hornbeam-leaf fold stacking replaces TSVs in memory stacks
idea: Hornbeam leaves fold along pleats inside the bud and open intact. Mount thinned DRAM dies on a roll-to-roll printed polyimide flex with fine copper wiring and fold it accordion-style so each die connects through the fold edge, giving an 8-16 die stack with no TSVs.
why: Avoids the TSV tax (~3x wafer area per bit, 20-30% yield loss in HBM); wide fold-edge buses can give HBM-class bandwidth at lower cost.

title: Aircraft anodizing tank grows billions of capacitor molds without lithography
idea: Aerospace anodizing self-organizes aluminum into hexagonal nanopore arrays with AR >1000:1 using only Al, acid and volts. Sputter Al on the wafer, nanoimprint a pre-texture that registers pores to the access-transistor grid, two-step anodize to 40-60 nm pitch, then ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN inside the pores.
why: Replaces EUV hole patterning and fluorocarbon high-AR plasma etch (facts 1, 4); AR 100:1+ pushes Cs well past today's ~5 fF wall.

title: Token-loop restoration: inference reads restore weights before they fade
idea: Inverts 'refresh must be a separate maintenance operation': lay out inference weights so every row is activated (and thus restored by its sense amplifier) once per decoding step (<20 ms) and remove refresh from those banks; if the token loop stalls, the read-only weights are dropped and re-streamed from flash.
why: Zero refresh power and ~10% bandwidth back in weight banks; the 20 ms retention target allows shorter capacitors with less mold and fluorocarbon etch per bit.

title: Self-replicating nanoimprint stamps make each memory layer cost cents
idea: Ideal: a mask that copies itself forever. Closest: write one e-beam quartz master per layer, replicate it into thousands of UV-cured polymer daughter stamps (and granddaughters from those), and use each daughter for ~100 roll-to-plate imprints on panels or wafers before recycling.
why: 100x: litho (5-7 EUV layers, depreciation ~55% of wafer cost, Fact 4) dominates; mask+exposure cost per layer goes from ~$0.5-1 per die-area-equivalent to <$0.01. Trades overlay (~10-20 nm) and defect accumulation across stamp generations (spare rows).

title: Display-scrap indium and gallium loop feeding oxide-semiconductor memory
idea: Box [feedstock: spent IGZO sputter targets + end-of-life panels | refining: acid leach + solvent extraction | product: targets and ALD precursors | buyer: BEOL oxide-memory fabs]: contract recyclers to recover In/Ga from spent targets (only ~30% of a target is consumed) and scrapped panels, and recast them as dedicated memory-grade feedstock.
why: In/Ga chokepoints (China ~60% In, ~98% Ga): spent targets alone return ~70% of purchased indium, securing feedstock if oxide-semiconductor DRAM scales.

title: Defense Production Act priority rating for semiconductor helium
idea: Within $1M/24 months: fund analysis and a coalition petition for DPA Title I priority ratings (DO/DX) on U.S.-produced helium, NF3 and WF6 deliveries to domestic memory fabs during declared shortages, with a fab-usage reporting template.
why: Shortage allocation is now first-come or contract-based; rated-order priority keeps U.S. DRAM lines running at negligible public cost.

title: Harvest and re-bin DRAM dies from retired servers
idea: Magnify each die's service life: retired hyperscaler DIMMs are retested at speed, re-binned by retention, and rebuilt into CXL expansion cards for cold tiers, with laser die-debond to rescue good dies from failed modules.
why: Each reused GB avoids ~1 GB of new wafer, EUV, helium and water. Millions of DIMMs retire every year while prices are up 4x.

title: Adiabatic charge-recovery wordline drivers borrowed from failed reversible computing
idea: Adiabatic logic died in CPUs because multiphase power clocks and slow ramps cost speed. DRAM wordlines are big, slow (5-10 ns), ~3 V capacitive lines, ideal for it: ramp each subarray's wordline to VPP through a 4-8 step tank-capacitor ladder and return the charge to the tanks on precharge.
why: Wordline CV2 at ~3 V is stuck (voltage floor); N-step charging cuts dissipation ~1/N (>60% at 4 steps) and shrinks VPP charge pumps in the periphery; energy is the resource saved.

title: Solar-cell spatial ALD multiplies hafnium and zirconium precursor utilization
idea: PERC solar lines deposit Al2O3 by spatial ALD, moving wafers under separated precursor zones instead of filling and purging a chamber. Adapt rotary-platen spatial ALD for DRAM ZrO2/HfO2/Al2O3 capacitor dielectrics and TiN electrodes and capture the unused metal-organic stream for re-synthesis; the capacitor stack and DDR/HBM interface stay identical.
why: Temporal ALD often uses only a few percent of costly precursor; spatial ALD can exceed ~30-50% utilization with 5-10x throughput, cutting Hf/Zr/Ti precursor demand and tool count.

title: Thinfilm's printed memory minus PFAS: croconic-acid ferroelectric crossbars on plastic
idea: Thin Film Electronics' printed memory used PVDF-TrFE, a PFAS-class fluoropolymer, and died at tens of bits per tag on low density and high-voltage switching. Use croconic acid (C5H2O5), a single-molecule organic ferroelectric with ~20 uC/cm2 room-temperature polarization, vapor-deposited below 150 C on PEN film and imprint-patterned into a crossbar with printed ZnO Schottky selectors.
why: Removes PFAS entirely; feedstock is C, H, O; low-temperature processing uses little energy; ferroelectric state needs no refresh. Targets an abundant cold-working-memory tier; switching speed and endurance are the physics risk.

title: Substitute vapor-deposited dry resist for spin-coat and aqueous develop
idea: Deposit metal-oxo (tin-oxide) photoresist from the vapor phase, expose, and develop it with a halide plasma in the same cluster tool, replacing spin coating, aqueous TMAH development and DI rinse.
why: Track develop and rinse is ~5-10% of fab UPW; the dry route cuts it >10x and also cuts resist chemical volume ~5x.

title: Substitute vapor-phase chelation for SC2 metal-contamination cleans
idea: Remove Fe, Cu and Ni contamination by exposing wafers to formic acid or acetylacetone vapor at 150-250 C, forming volatile metal formate or acac complexes that are pumped away, replacing HCl/H2O2/H2O SC2 baths and rinses.
why: Metal cleans are a major recurring wet step; dry chelation drops their water >20x and removes hydrogen peroxide and HCl supply from the step.

title: Bitcoin-miner siting: DRAM fabs at stranded hydro and flare gas
idea: Crypto miners chase stranded megawatts in Pacific Northwest hydro, Texas flare gas and curtailed wind. Site new U.S. DRAM capacity at those nodes with interruptible-load contracts covering deferrable loads (abatement, UPW heating, test and burn-in) and cold-climate free cooling for chillers.
why: Energy is a growing share of wafer cost under EUV: buying at <$30/MWh and skipping grid-queue delays could halve power cost and shorten time to power.

title: Zirconium disulfide channel with its own oxide as gate dielectric
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise: 2D ZrS2 (bandgap ~1.7 eV) oxidizes easily, which is normally a defect. Here a controlled O2 plasma deliberately converts the top layers into amorphous ZrO2 (k ~20) that serves as a perfect-interface gate dielectric, giving a 2-3 layer ZrS2 write transistor for a 2T0C gain cell.
why: Replaces IGZO (In, Ga) in capacitor-less gain cells with Zr, S and O only. An atomically thin channel with native high-k targets sub-aA leakage at <=400 C, compatible with stacking 3D tiers.

title: Atmospheric spatial ALD on moving webs: no vacuum, no helium
idea: Ideal: atomic-precision films made in open air. Closest: spatial-ALD heads with gas-bearing-separated precursor zones (TMA/H2O, DEZ/H2O, TiCl4/H2O) coat 1-2 m webs or panels at 1-5 m/min at atmospheric pressure, laying down gate oxide, capacitor dielectric and ZnO channel with no vacuum chambers, He backside cooling or PFAS chamber cleans.
why: 100x path: deposition is ~20-25% of fab capex and spatial-ALD tool cost per m2/hr is ~100x below cluster ALD, a pillar of ~$0.1/GB panel/foil memory. Trades film density and dielectric leakage (more refresh).

title: Per-recipe scarcity ledger that feeds back into process engineering
idea: TRIZ #23 Feedback: meter each tool's use per wafer of He, ALD precursors, fluorinated gases, UPW and kWh. Price each at a shadow scarcity cost (e.g., helium at its outage price) inside the fab's cost-per-bit model, so recipe changes are scored and rewarded on scarce-resource reduction.
why: Sustained sub-metering feedback has delivered 20-40% resource cuts in energy programs. This applies the same loop to every chokepoint input at once.

title: Surface-activated room-temperature bonding stacks memory layers without solder
idea: Effect: dangling-bond covalent adhesion. An argon fast-atom beam strips native oxides so Cu-Cu and SiO2-SiO2 surfaces fuse at room temperature in vacuum, stacking thinned DRAM or oxide-memory layers at <1 um pitch with no Sn-Ag microbumps, underfill or 400 C bonding anneal.
why: HBM TSV/microbump tax (fact 6), Ag/Sn and fluorinated underfills; denser vertical links at room temperature.

title: Po DRAM on dirty silicon: metallurgical substrate plus thick epi
idea: Po: 'DRAM is built on dirty silicon.' Extracted: use cheap upgraded-metallurgical-grade (~5N) cast silicon as a mechanical substrate, add a heavily doped gettering and diffusion-barrier buried layer, then grow a thick epitaxial device layer from electronic-grade trichlorosilane, so only the top ~10 um needs 11N purity.
why: Electronic-grade polysilicon (Siemens process ~50-100 kWh/kg, few suppliers) and high-purity quartz crucibles largely bypassed; substrate cost and energy cut several-fold.

title: On-site electrochemical persulfate regeneration closes the sulfuric loop
idea: Periodic-table walk, S (16): electrolyze spent sulfuric acid on boron-doped-diamond anodes to regenerate peroxydisulfate continuously, so the cleaning oxidant is remade on-site rather than consuming fresh H2SO4 and H2O2.
why: ~90% less sulfuric/peroxide purchase and wastewater; fluorine-free; uses only S, O, H and C/B electrodes.

title: Pyroelectric non-destructive readout of boron-aluminum-nitride ferroelectric cells
idea: Effect: pyroelectricity. Store bits in wurtzite Al(1-x)B(x)N ferroelectric capacitors (no Hf, no Sc) and read them without switching: a ~5 K heat pulse from a wordline micro-heater makes a pyro-current whose sign gives the polarization. Because the signal is only hundreds of electrons, an in-cell gain transistor senses it.
why: Destructive read (fact 8) and Hf/Sc dependence: endurance is limited only by writes, and Al, B and N are abundant and U.S.-sourced.

title: Indium-free, gallium-free ALD tin-oxide access transistors
idea: Box [stacked MIM cap | 4 nm ALD SnO2 vertical channel TFT | voltage SA | BEOL monolithic 1T1C over CMOS | logic wafer | thermal ALD]: replace IGZO with an ultrathin ALD SnO2 channel whose carrier density is set by oxygen-vacancy control and an O3 post-treatment, giving oxide-class off-current with only tin and oxygen.
why: Gallium (China ~98%, export-controlled) and indium chokepoints of oxide-semiconductor DRAM: keeps oxide-TFT ultra-low leakage (refresh cut >100x) while using tin from diversified sources.

title: RF SiGe quantum wells hold holes in a floating-body cell
idea: Adapt the bandgap-engineered SiGe base of RF heterojunction transistors by burying a thin SiGe quantum well below a vertical-channel transistor. Holes generated by band-to-band tunneling collect in the well and shift the threshold, and the valence-band offset stretches retention far beyond plain floating-body cells.
why: A capacitor-free bit in bulk silicon plus a few % germanium, avoiding the capacitor etch and dielectric. The germanium can come from US zinc-smelter residues.

title: Point-of-use helium micro-recovery skid on tool exhaust
idea: Within $1M/24 months: build a refrigerator-sized skid that taps the foreline of He-backside etch and CVD tools, separates He from the N2 purge with a hollow-fiber membrane plus a small PSA stage, and returns 99.99% He to the chuck supply; pilot it on 3 tools.
why: Captures ~60-80% of per-tool helium while Qatar's ~30% is offline, with payback in months at shortage prices and no fab-wide liquefier.

title: Anhydrous HF vapor and atomic hydrogen replace ultrapure-water cleans
idea: Clean targets are ~1e9-1e10 contaminant atoms/cm2, nanograms per wafer, yet each wafer consumes thousands of litres of UPW. Convert pre-deposition cleans to anhydrous HF/NH3 vapor oxide removal, remote atomic hydrogen for carbon and UV/O3 for organics, keeping one megasonic water rinse per module for particles.
why: Cuts UPW per wafer ~40-60% plus the energy of making it, and shrinks HF-laden wastewater.

title: Thin-film transfluxor cells that compute while reading, ferrite-only materials
idea: Revive RCA's 1956 transfluxor: sputter NiZn-ferrite rings with one large and one small aperture in BEOL. The stored blocked/unblocked flux state of the outer leg decides whether a drive on the small aperture induces an output, giving non-destructive read plus AND/inhibit logic in the same element, so rows can be filtered before any data leaves the array.
why: Data movement (fact 5) and overfetch (fact 8) through in-place filtering; built only from Fe, Ni, Zn, O and Cu (no Hf, W, Pt or In); claims 5-10x less data shipped for scan and filter workloads.

title: Drum-style lockstep weight broadcast replaces replicated HBM weight copies
idea: Revive the magnetic-drum principle, where data circulates past many fixed heads: keep ONE copy of model weights in a pod-level pool and stream it every token step over a DWDM optical broadcast (passive 1:64 splitters). All inference replicas consume the same rotating stream in lockstep and hold only a small sliding window locally. A 100 GB model at 50 steps/s needs ~40 Tb/s, about four 100-channel fibers.
why: Uses less of the scarce resource, DRAM itself: replicated-serving pods keep up to 64 identical weight copies in HBM, and broadcasting frees 40-70% of HBM capacity for KV cache, like adding supply without any wafers.

title: Magnesium-zinc-silicon oxide replaces IGZO in gain cells
idea: TRIZ #40 Composite materials, giving each IGZO job to an abundant cation: Zn 4s orbitals provide the conduction path (indium's role), Si binds oxygen strongly to suppress vacancies (gallium's role), and Mg widens the gap to ~4 eV for lower leakage. The amorphous Mg-Zn-Si-O channel is deposited by ALD supercycles.
why: Removes In (byproduct-limited) and Ga (China ~98%) from oxide-semiconductor DRAM roadmaps at equal or lower off-current. Its ~5-15 cm2/Vs mobility is enough for write transistors.

title: Refresh-free silicon-carbide DRAM in existing U.S. SiC power fabs
idea: Ideal: memory that never refreshes, made of silicon and carbon. Closest: 4H-SiC 1T1C cells (3.26 eV gap, generation leakage ~1e-19 of Si; 1990s demos showed multi-year room-temperature retention) built on 200 mm SiC lines in North Carolina/New York idled by the power-SiC glut.
why: Removes refresh (16-33% of idle power, 10-20% of bandwidth, Fact 3) using only Si, C and common dopants and idle U.S. capacity; density lags (larger F), so targets always-on low-power tiers.

title: Lunar-base abundant-element PDK: a gain cell from only eight elements
idea: A Moon-base fab could use only regolith-abundant elements, so impose that rule in a university nanofab: build a 2T gain-cell array from Si, O, N, Al, Ti and H (plus B/P dopants) only, with poly-Si channels, LPCVD SiO2/Si3N4, ALD Al2O3, sputtered Al and TiN, and contact lithography on 100 mm wafers. Benchmark retention against a W/ZrO2 reference.
why: Proves a chokepoint-free memory process (no W, Hf, Zr, Ta, Co, In or Ga) and gives a template for a resource-proof U.S. DRAM tier.

title: Periphery wafer from U.S. legacy fabs bonded onto cell array
idea: Combine image-sensor wafer bonding with DRAM: build sense amps, decoders and I/O on 28-40 nm logic wafers in existing U.S. mature fabs and only the array on the DRAM wafer; the array wafer adds exactly one mask (hybrid-bond pads) and drops its periphery masks.
why: Periphery is ~49% of the die; moving it to EUV-free, depreciated U.S. fabs cuts DRAM-fab area per bit ~40% and frees the array from periphery thermal budget.

title: CCD serial memory revived in idle CMOS image-sensor fabs
idea: Revive Fairchild/Intel's 1975 CCD memory: build buried-channel two-phase CCD loops, where data recirculates and is regenerated every lap, at 65-90 nm on image-sensor lines, as a sequential tier for weight streaming and KV-cache scans.
why: No EUV, no capacitor pillars, no Hf or W; uses mature 300 mm sensor capacity at ~4F2 per bit at relaxed F; claims 3x cheaper per bit than DDR for streaming access.

title: Esaki tunnel-diode latch cells in plain silicon
idea: Inverts 'a DRAM bit needs a storage capacitor': pair two degenerately doped silicon tunnel diodes (negative differential resistance) with one access transistor so the storage node sits at one of two stable points held by the NDR valley current, a static cell with no refresh.
why: Zero refresh and no capacitor (no pillars, Hf/Zr, Ru or high-AR fluorocarbon etch); only silicon and dopants; standby set by a ~pA valley current target.

title: MRI zero-boil-off logic: per-tool helium recapture and reliquefaction
idea: Borrowing from MRI magnets that went 'zero boil-off' with cold-head recondensers: fit every etch/deposition cluster with a helium recapture manifold on electrostatic-chuck backside-gas leak paths, load-lock purges and leak-check exhaust, feeding a small cryocooler purifier that recompresses or reliquefies He for reuse. Fab helium becomes a closed inventory topped up a few percent per month instead of a consumable.
why: Qatar's ~30% of helium supply has been offline since March 2026; recapture cuts purchased helium per wafer by ~80-90% and decouples DRAM output from the helium chokepoint.

title: Skip the deuterium anneal; let ECC cover the trap tail
idea: Reverse the final passivation step: omit the high-pressure deuterium/H2 interface anneal, accept the ~1% of access transistors with extra trap-assisted leakage, and correct them with ECC.
why: Removes deuterium (heavy-water derived, few suppliers) and a high-pressure furnace step.

title: 2050 engineer: rutile titania on tin-oxide electrodes, no hafnium
idea: Persona: a 2050 engineer who sees Hf, Zr and Ru as a passing habit. Grow rutile-phase TiO2 (k ~90-110) below 400 C on an antimony-doped SnO2 bottom electrode, whose rutile structure templates the high-k phase. Add 2 nm Al-doped interlayers to suppress leakage.
why: Removes hafnium, zirconium and the usual ruthenium template. k ~100 versus ~40 means the target Cs is reached at aspect ratio ~30:1 instead of 60-75:1 (fact 1).

title: Rutile TiO2 high-k grown on niobium-doped tin-oxide template electrodes
idea: Jump to the atomic lattice: rutile SnO2 matches rutile TiO2 within ~3%. A conductive Nb- or Ta-doped SnO2 bottom electrode therefore templates ALD TiO2 into its rutile phase (k ~80-100) at low temperature without Ru/RuO2, and Al doping of the TiO2 suppresses leakage.
why: Delivers the k ~70+ needed to break the capacitor charge wall using Ti, Sn and Nb instead of Hf/Zr and Ru. Holding 5 fF lets AR fall from ~70:1 to ~35:1.

title: Skull-melting crystal puller: silicon grows its own crucible
idea: Borrowed from titanium and zirconia skull melting: a water-cooled segmented copper cold crucible with RF induction holds the silicon melt inside a frozen silicon skin, so no quartz crucible ever touches the melt; a magnetic cusp field stirs and shapes the melt for 300 mm Czochralski pulls. The crucible is permanent and only electricity is consumed.
why: Eliminates the Spruce Pine high-purity quartz crucible (>80% concentrated, consumed every 1-2 ingots) and yields oxygen-free crystals with fewer thermal donors and leakage-tail defects; costs ~2-3x melt energy, offset by zero crucible spend and longer continuous pulls.

title: Po memory sold by the square meter: DRAM tiles on display glass
idea: Po: 'memory is sold by the square meter like carpet.' Extracted: run oxide-TFT gain-cell arrays on Gen-8.5 (2.2 x 2.5 m) display glass in under-used LCD fabs, then cut the panel into memory tiles mounted beside processors. One panel has ~80x the area of a 300 mm wafer and uses no single-crystal silicon, no quartz crucible and no EUV.
why: Capital intensity and crucible/polysilicon intensity: display-fab cost per cm2 is several times lower than DRAM-wafer cost per cm2, so a low-density capacity tier could still be competitive in bits per capital dollar. It also brings a non-DRAM industry's idle capacity into memory.

title: Inkjet-head e-beam writer: 10,000 beamlets pattern without EUV
idea: Inkjet heads fire thousands of nozzles in parallel; build U.S. multi-column electron-beam direct writers with MEMS beam-blanker arrays that write DRAM critical layers straight into resist, replacing EUV exposures with a mask-free step.
why: EUV has one foreign supplier and each tool draws ~1 MW with tin plasma and hydrogen; a domestic multibeam writer removes EUV, masks and pellicles and can write per-wafer redundancy maps.

title: Pulp-mill chlorine-free bleaching chemistry replaces sulfuric-peroxide wafer cleans
idea: Paper mills replaced chlorine bleaching with totally chlorine-free ozone/peroxide sequences. Adapt that sequence: replace SPM (piranha) resist strips and SC-1 cleans with ozonated DI water carrying dissolved CO2, followed by UV-activated peroxide, all generated on site from oxygen, water and electricity.
why: Fabs buy thousands of tonnes a year of 96% sulfuric acid and peroxide. Ozone chemistry cuts purchased chemical mass ~80%, along with trucking and neutralization load.

title: Diatomaceous-earth frustules as printed 3D capacitor scaffolds
idea: Diatom shells are nanoporous silica lattices with huge surface area. Print a paste of size-sorted diatomaceous earth (mined in Nevada and California) onto foil, coat it roll-to-roll by spatial ALD with electrode-dielectric-electrode, and use each frustule cluster as a 20-50x area-enhanced storage capacitor.
why: Gives DRAM-like charge per footprint in printed memory without HAR etching or EUV, from a mineral that costs cents per kg.

title: WWII high-speed-steel swap: molybdenum replaces tungsten in wordlines
idea: During WWII tungsten shortages, toolmakers replaced T-series tungsten high-speed steels with M-series molybdenum steels that cut just as well. Replace W in buried wordlines, bitline contacts and periphery plugs with Mo from fluorine-free MoO2Cl2/MoCl5 precursors, whose shorter electron mean free path beats W below 15 nm; the die keeps its standard DDR5/HBM pinout, timing and JEDEC qualification.
why: Tungsten is ~80% Chinese while the U.S. is a top molybdenum producer (Colorado mines); removes WF6/HF and trims wordline RC ~10-20% with nothing visible to the memory controller.

title: Veneer peeling: slice twenty thin wafers from one crystal
idea: Plywood mills peel thin veneers from a log; peel 20-50 um device-grade silicon layers from a thick CZ donor by stress-induced spalling or porous-silicon lift-off, bond each onto a reusable or glass handle, and repolish the donor for the next peel, so one prime wafer yields 15-25 device layers.
why: DRAM uses only the top ~5 um of a 775 um wafer; this cuts CZ ingots, quartz crucibles, polysilicon and growth energy per wafer ~10x and removes wire-saw kerf (~40% of each crystal).

title: Substitute gas-cluster ion beams for slurry chemical-mechanical polishing
idea: Planarize with location-specific gas-cluster ion beams (Ar/NF3 clusters of ~1000 atoms) steered by an in-line thickness map, combined with spin-on planarizing film plus selective plasma etch-back, replacing CMP slurries and post-CMP brush and megasonic cleans.
why: CMP plus post-CMP cleaning is ~15-30% of fab UPW; dry planarization cuts that >10x and removes ceria/silica slurry waste.

title: Lego: partial-good DRAM dies stitched into reduced-capacity modules
idea: Stimulus 'Lego' (odd bricks still build things) -> a 10-person assembly shop buys wafer-sort rejects with one dead bank or sub-array, maps bad regions on an FPGA tester and builds modules whose controller firmware fences the bad addresses, sold as reduced-capacity memory.
why: Recovers silicon whose helium, energy and water were already spent on scrapped dies; adds several percent to effective supply.

title: 1990s BST capacitor revived with US-molybdenum SrMoO3 electrodes
idea: Revive the abandoned gigabit-era barium-strontium-titanate capacitor (k~200-300) using conductive perovskite SrMoO3 electrodes, with molybdenum mined in Colorado, instead of Pt/Ru. The dielectric grows lattice-matched without a low-k dead layer.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): k~200 gives 5 fF at an aspect ratio of ~20 instead of 70, removing Hf/Zr, Ru/Pt and much of the deep fluorocarbon etch; claims ~30% fewer cell process steps.

title: Four charge levels per capacitor double bits per gram
idea: Magnify bits per cell 2x: store four charge levels in each capacitor and read them with a two-step successive-approximation sense amplifier against a reference bitline, with tighter refresh for the top level.
why: If margins hold, halves silicon, W/Mo, Hf/Zr and EUV exposure per bit; a direct cost-per-bit lever.

title: Tea bag: chelating cartridges leach hafnium, ruthenium, tantalum from shields
idea: Stimulus 'tea bag' (steep, then lift out the goodness) -> steep used PVD/ALD chamber shields and target backing plates in mild oxidizing baths and pass the leachate through selective chelating-resin cartridges (hydroxamate for Hf/Zr, thiourea for Ru) to recover metal for target and precursor remanufacture.
why: 60-80% of sputtered or ALD metal ends up on shields and targets, not wafers; closing the loop could halve primary Hf/Ru/Ta demand.

title: Eliminate neon excimer gas: all-solid-state 193 nm lithography laser
idea: Generate 193 nm light from high-power Yb fiber lasers via frequency conversion and sum-frequency mixing in CLBO crystals, replacing ArF excimer chambers that consume Ne/Ar/F2 gas fills.
why: Removes the neon chokepoint (historically ~50% Ukraine/Russia) and F2 handling for the dozens of DUV immersion layers DRAM still uses; less tool downtime.

title: Po memory that never shrinks: perpetual-node legacy DRAM franchise
idea: Po: 'memory that never shrinks.' Extracted: freeze a copy-exact 180-150 nm DRAM process for 20+ years and sell long-life legacy parts (SDR to DDR3, small densities, industrial, auto and defense) under take-or-pay supply contracts, so those markets stop consuming leading-edge wafers and end-of-life buys.
why: Effective supply: legacy-DRAM end-of-life notices fed the 2025-26 price spikes; a perpetual U.S. node moves those bits off leading-edge capacity with no mask or node R&D churn and ~0 depreciation after year 5.

title: Fab-side closed tungsten loop from exhaust and spent targets
idea: Periodic-table walk, W (74): cryo-trap unreacted WF6 from W-CVD exhaust and redistill it, and send spent targets, shields and chamber scrap to zinc-process reclamation under a fab take-back contract.
why: W is ~80% China; recapture could cut virgin W per wafer by ~50%.

title: Porcelain enameling: borax-glaze BCN barrier replaces tantalum liners
idea: Enamelers fuse borax glazes to steel as impermeable barriers; deposit a ~1-2 nm amorphous boron-carbon-nitride 'glaze' from precursors made from California borax as the copper diffusion barrier and liner in DRAM metal layers, replacing Ta/TaN.
why: Tantalum comes from conflict-mineral regions; a thinner barrier also frees conductor cross-section for ~20-30% lower line resistance at tight pitch.

title: Pearl: area-selective ALD grows dielectric only inside capacitor holes
idea: Stimulus 'pearl' (nacre grows only around the grit) -> dose a small-molecule inhibitor that blankets top surfaces but cannot diffuse into 60:1 holes, so ZrO2/HfO2 grows only inside; pair with a cold-trap recirculation loop that condenses unreacted metal-amide precursor for reuse.
why: ALD precursor utilization is typically <5%; this cuts Hf/Zr precursor use 5-10x and removes an etch-back step.

title: Silicatein-catalysed titanate dielectric grown inside capacitor holes
idea: Marine sponges grow glass spicules with the enzyme silicatein, which also turns titanium and barium alkoxides into crystalline oxides at room temperature. Immobilize a silicatein-mimetic serine-histidine catalytic monolayer on the TiN bottom electrode so a water-borne Sr/Ba-Ti precursor bath deposits conformal SrTiO3 (k~100+) only on catalytic surfaces, then crystallize it with a short anneal.
why: Replaces Hf/Zr metalorganic ALD (Hf is a nuclear-Zr byproduct; precursors are <10% utilized) and pushes k toward the ~70 needed to beat the ~5 fF charge wall at a lower aspect ratio.

title: ETA-10 lesson: liquid-nitrogen-immersed DRAM pods that need no refresh
idea: ETA Systems' LN2-cooled supercomputer died on per-board cryostat logistics, frost and service cost, not physics. Fix exactly that with sealed rack-scale LN2 immersion tanks fed by an on-site air-separation reliquefier (closed loop, no venting); at 77 K DRAM leakage falls ~1e6x so refresh disappears, and new cells can use ~4x smaller capacitors (~20:1 aspect ratio, plain Al2O3/SiO2 dielectric).
why: Kills refresh (~46 fJ/bit, 16-33% of idle power, 10-20% bandwidth) and lets capacitors drop high-k Zr/Hf and 60-75:1 etching; coolant is nitrogen (78% of air) instead of Qatar-exposed helium; cooler, faster wires partially repay the cryo energy.

title: Reusable silicon-nitride crucible replaces Spruce Pine quartz in Czochralski pulling
idea: Periodic-table walk, Si+N (14,7): pull DRAM crystals from dense reaction-bonded Si3N4 crucibles with a sacrificial Si3N4 powder release coat (borrowed from multicrystalline solar casting); no cristobalite devitrification, so one crucible survives ~10 pulls with continuous recharge, and oxygen for gettering is dosed via O2 in the Ar ambient instead of crucible dissolution.
why: Removes most high-purity-quartz demand (>80% from one US district); slight N doping (1e14-1e15 cm^-3) even helps vacancy control in DRAM wafers.

title: Proton-relay croconic acid: fluorine-free printed ferroelectric charge booster
idea: Enzymes and bacteriorhodopsin move charge along hydrogen-bonded proton wires. Croconic acid crystals switch polarization by the same proton tautomerism (~20 uC/cm2, no fluorine); inkjet-print them as the cell capacitor and run them in a volatile minor-loop mode that adds displacement charge without full switching, to protect endurance.
why: Replaces fluorinated P(VDF-TrFE) (a PFAS) and Hf-based ferroelectrics in printed memory, with ~5x more stored charge than linear printed dielectrics at a 150 C process.

title: Ephemeral memory: data dies before charge does, so never refresh
idea: Inverts 'stored data must outlive cell retention': a refresh-less DRAM tier holds only AI activations, gradients, KV blocks and packet buffers whose lifetime the compiler/runtime proves is below a guaranteed 10-50 ms retention, with hardware write-timestamps that fault any read past the deadline.
why: Zero refresh power in that tier; cells can use ~30:1 instead of 70:1 capacitors, roughly halving mold, fluorocarbon etch gas and ALD precursor per bit, and refresh counters vanish from the periphery.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching carves 150:1 silicon capacitor trenches
idea: Box [MIS trench cap in bulk Si | vertical Si access | voltage SA | revived trench-capacitor 1T1C | CZ Si | NIL-patterned electroless Ag mesh + HF/H2O2 metal-assisted chemical etch]: the Ag catalyst sinks vertically in the HF/H2O2 bath, cutting 30 nm holes at >150:1 aspect ratio with no plasma; the holes are then lined with ALD dielectric and doped poly.
why: Capacitor charge wall (needs AR ~115): a wet, room-temperature etch reaches AR 150+ with almost no tool capex, replacing high-AR plasma etchers that need Ar/He dilution and backside cooling; the Ag is recovered from the bath.

title: Po memory from four common elements: HSG polysilicon ONO capacitor
idea: Po: 'the cell contains only silicon, oxygen, nitrogen and phosphorus.' Extracted: revive the late-1990s stacked capacitor with hemispherical-grain rugged polysilicon electrodes (2-2.5x area), a thin nitrided oxide-nitride dielectric and doped-poly plugs, removing TiN, Ru, Zr, Hf and W from the cell.
why: Scarce-resource intensity: zero chokepoint metals in the array, fully U.S.-manufacturable on 200 mm tools; density is modest but material supply risk falls to ~0.

title: Substitute self-passivating MAX-phase conductor for tungsten bitlines and barriers
idea: Sputter Ti3AlC2/Ti2AlC nanolaminate bitlines and crystallize by laser anneal; aluminum in the lattice self-forms a ~1 nm Al2O3 sidewall skin that acts as liner and diffusion barrier, removing separate TiN barriers and WF6 chemistry.
why: Abundant Ti, Al and C replace tungsten; one conductor/barrier film with short electron mean free path suffers little size-effect resistivity rise, and a thinner liner lowers bitline capacitance and sense energy.

title: Eliminate the Boltzmann tax: all-silicon bilayer tunnel-FET periphery at 0.3 V
idea: Build decoders, sense control and datapath from electron-hole bilayer tunnel FETs in silicon (no Ge or III-V indium), whose band-to-band switching allows sub-60 mV/decade slopes and a 0.3 V supply.
why: Periphery is ~49% of the die and much of the access energy; 0.3 V versus 1.1 V cuts its CV2 ~13x.

title: Bell Labs ferroelectric matrix fixed by co-fired ZnO varistor selectors
idea: 1950s Bell Labs barium-titanate matrix memory died on half-select disturb because BaTiO3 has no sharp switching threshold. Co-fire a multilayer ceramic stack on the MLCC process (hundreds of ~0.5 um layers) where each BaTiO3 cell sits in series with a ZnO varistor layer (nonlinearity >30) that blocks half-select voltages.
why: MLCC lines already make trillions of BaTiO3/nickel parts a year with no wafer, EUV or helium; Ba, Ti, Zn, Ni are abundant; ferroelectric storage is nonvolatile; density limited by printed electrode pitch, offset by layer count.

title: Deuterated-drug kinetic isotope effect hardens access-transistor interfaces
idea: Deuterated drugs slow metabolism because C-D bonds break more slowly than C-H. Replace the forming-gas H2 anneal with high-pressure D2 from Canadian heavy-water stocks so Si-D bonds passivate the access-transistor and STI-edge interfaces and resist hot-carrier and GIDL-stress depassivation; DDR/HBM refresh commands are unchanged, on-die refresh management simply tracks fewer weak rows.
why: Fact 3: the leakage tail forces refresh (16-33% of idle power); a tighter, longer-lived tail lets retention bins relax ~1.5-2x and cuts burn-in screening loss.

title: Scuba rebreather loop recycles excimer-laser neon in DUV scanners
idea: Closed-circuit rebreathers scrub contaminants and recirculate the diluent gas. Put a getter and cryo-purification loop on every ArF/KrF excimer laser to strip fluorine-reaction contaminants (HF, CF4, O2) from the ~96% neon buffer and re-inject it, topping up F2 from onsite electrolysis; only litho tools change, DDR/HBM products do not.
why: Neon came mostly from Ukrainian and Russian steel-plant air separation; DRAM runs many DUV immersion layers, and recirculation cuts neon purchases ~90%.

title: Harvest DRAM dies from retired servers into CXL memory pools
idea: Charge storage causes no atomic change, so DRAM has no wear-out and a retired DIMM's dies still embody every scarce input. Desolder and retest dies at scale, rebin by speed and retention, and repackage them into CXL Type-3 expanders with stronger ECC and patrol scrub as tier-2 memory.
why: Adds ~10-20% of annual DRAM bit supply with zero new wafers, helium, quartz or tungsten, as a US remanufacturing business.

title: Plated-wire memory reborn as drawn multimaterial fiber woven into crossbars
idea: Plated-wire memory put the storage film on a beryllium-copper wire substrate and died on per-wire plating cost and coarse pitch. Thermally draw a glass/polymer preform containing conductor, charge-storage sheath and semiconductor layers into kilometers of 20-50 um fiber (multimaterial fiber drawing), then weave orthogonal fibers so each warp-weft crossing is a cell.
why: No wafer, lithography or EUV: a $1-2M draw tower makes km of device per hour from grams of preform; removes beryllium; ~1-2 GB/m2 of fabric, stackable in layers.

title: Widrow memistor revival: electroplated analog weights in solid electrolyte
idea: Revive Bernard Widrow's 1960 memistor, a three-terminal cell that plates copper onto a carbon resistor: use a PFAS-free copper-doped phosphosilicate-glass electrolyte so a separate write terminal plates or strips copper while the read terminal senses resistance. Each cell holds a 6-bit analog weight and multiplies in place.
why: One cell replaces six DRAM bits of frozen weights and computes in situ (fact 5); uses only Cu, C, P and Si; separate read and write paths give unlimited read endurance; claims 4-6x fewer DRAM bits for inference weights.

title: Williams tube on glass: field-emitter arrays read and refresh charge dots
idea: The Williams tube stored bits as charge spots on a CRT face and died on drift, bulk and constant regeneration; Candescent's field-emission display died on vacuum spacers and panel cost. Fuse them: a thin vacuum-sealed glass panel where gated carbon or Mo emitter arrays address an opposing grid of dielectric charge dots, reading by secondary-emission current and regenerating each frame.
why: Cells contain no transistor, no Hf/Zr dielectric and no tungsten plug; periphery is the emitter row/column matrix; built from glass, carbon or Mo and oxide films on retired FED/plasma panel lines.

title: Mine the fab's own WF6 exhaust as tungsten ore
idea: Tungsten CVD deposits only ~20-40% of delivered WF6, so scrubber streams carry W far richer than ore (~0.5% WO3). Trap exhaust in alkaline scrubbers as sodium tungstate, ion-exchange to ammonium paratungstate, calcine to WO3 and re-fluorinate with on-site F2 back to WF6.
why: Cuts new tungsten demand per wafer ~50-60% and turns the remainder into a US-domestic loop against China's ~80% share.

title: Bonded 4H-SiC film access transistors erase the refresh leakage tail
idea: Generation leakage scales with intrinsic carrier density ni ~ exp(-Eg/2kT); 4H-SiC (3.26 eV) has ni ~1e-9 cm-3 versus 1e10 for Si, collapsing the 13 fA junction tail by many orders. Activate implants in a SiC wafer at 1600 C first, Smart-Cut a 100 nm film onto the DRAM wafer, and build access transistors in it under the capacitor process.
why: Fact 3: retention moves from 64 ms toward hours, deleting ~46 fJ/bit refresh and 10-20% bandwidth loss; SiC is Si+C and US-made. SiO2/SiC interface traps and mobility are the risk.

title: Panel-scale DRAM: oxide-TFT 1T1C arrays on Gen-8.5 LCD glass
idea: Box [MIM cap | IGZO TFT | off-panel Si sense-amp chiplets | panel-level fan-out | 2.2x2.5 m glass | LCD-line photolithography]: fabricate relaxed-pitch (F~1 um) oxide-TFT 1T1C arrays on idle, depreciated LCD lines, dice into tiles and flip-chip Si sense/periphery chiplets at panel level for a capacity tier.
why: Capital/EUV and crucible intensity: F=1 um gives ~16 Mb/cm2, so one 5.5 m2 panel holds ~100 GB with no EUV and no crystalline-Si array; low density limits it to slow capacity tiers.

title: Post-package-repair rescue line for returned DIMMs
idea: Within $1M/24 months: write open firmware that runs exhaustive row-retention and hammer tests on returned and failing DDR4/DDR5 modules, then permanently remaps bad rows through JEDEC hard post-package-repair fuses and re-certifies modules that would otherwise be shredded.
why: A few failing rows now scrap whole modules; rescuing ~50-70% of returns adds supply with zero materials and yields field data on retention tails.

title: Po wordlines drawn in pencil: intercalated graphene buried wordlines
idea: Po: 'wordlines are drawn with a pencil.' Extracted: form buried wordlines from multilayer graphene precipitated at <500 C from a sacrificial nickel liner, then intercalate with FeCl3 or bromine to drop sheet resistance; graphene's resistivity does not rise at sub-10 nm widths the way tungsten's does from surface scattering.
why: Tungsten chokepoint (China ~80%) and WF6 fluorine chemistry removed from wordlines; at ~10 nm widths intercalated graphene could match or beat tungsten's effective resistivity, keeping wordline RC flat as cells shrink.

title: FeCl3-intercalated multilayer graphene bitlines replace ruthenium
idea: Worsen: move narrow bitlines and contacts to ruthenium mined almost entirely in South Africa and Russia. Flip: grow multilayer graphene at low temperature on sacrificial Co/Ni catalyst lines, then intercalate it with FeCl3 to raise carrier density, so its resistivity at <20 nm width beats Cu and rivals Ru.
why: PGM chokepoint and bitline RC: carbon is unlimited, with ~2x lower line RC than Cu at narrow widths claimed.

title: Intercalated multilayer graphene wordlines grown by nickel-mediated precipitation
idea: Effect: charge-transfer intercalation doping. Carbon diffuses through a Ni film at ~350 C and precipitates as multilayer graphene in trenches (layer exchange). FeCl3 intercalation then shifts the Fermi level and cuts resistivity toward Cu, giving barrier-free, electromigration-proof wordlines made of carbon.
why: Tungsten (China ~80%) and WF6; no liner volume at 10-15 nm and abundant feedstock, all below 400 C.

title: Turn idle display fabs into oxide-TFT memory foundries
idea: Rearrange industries: run oxide-TFT gain-cell memory arrays on Gen-8.5 glass panels in under-utilized LCD/OLED backplane lines, then dice and hybrid-bond the panels onto small CMOS periphery chiplets.
why: Uses glass (no crystal silicon, no HPQ crucibles, no EUV) and already-depreciated tools; Gen-8.5 panel area is ~25x a 300 mm wafer, attacking capital intensity and time-to-capacity.

title: Remote-plasma atomic-oxygen oxidation retires quartz furnaces at 400 C
idea: Effect: radical-driven oxidation kinetics. Atomic oxygen from a microwave or ICP remote plasma oxidizes and nitrides silicon at 300-400 C with near-thermal interface quality (Dit ~1e10/cm2eV). Gate, liner and isolation oxides come from single-wafer chambers instead of 900 C batch furnaces.
why: Quartz consumables (furnace tubes, boats, liners) and furnace energy; enables a furnace-free fab under the 400 C ceiling.

title: Gate-coupled thyristor: a self-latching pure-silicon bit
idea: Inverts 'a cell is passive and must be topped up from outside': a vertical PNPN thyristor with a gate-coupled base latches on or off by its own regenerative gain; a low-gain design holds 'on' cells at sub-pA holding current and 'off' cells draw nothing, so no refresh cycle exists.
why: Zero refresh power; no capacitor, no high-k, fewer metal layers; a pure-silicon 4-6F2 cell buildable in older US fabs.

title: Water-vapor plasma activated hybrid bonding for HBM stacks
idea: Box [HBM DRAM dies | standard | standard | bumpless Cu-SiCN hybrid-bonded HBM | Si | H2O/N2 low-power plasma activation + formic-acid vapor Cu-oxide reduction + 250 C anneal]: hydroxyl-terminate the SiCN with water-vapor plasma and reduce Cu oxide chemically instead of using Ar/N2 plasma activation or Ar sputter cleaning.
why: HBM TSV/microbump tax (3x area, 20-30% yield loss): bumpless bonding cuts pitch ~10x and removes underfill, with no argon in the flow.

title: Zinc-tin-oxide gain cells: indium- and gallium-free, fixing ZTO's display failure
idea: ZTO lost to IGZO in displays because it resisted wet etching selectively against source-drain metals and its bias-stress threshold drift shifted pixel gray levels. In a 2T gain cell on glass neither matters: pattern ZTO by chlorine dry etch, and since every cell is rewritten each refresh interval, threshold drift is erased; off-currents near 1e-19 A/um give seconds-to-minutes retention.
why: Removes gallium (China export controls since 2023) and indium from oxide memory; zinc and tin have diversified supply; long retention cuts refresh energy ~100x versus silicon DRAM.

title: Po the crucible is brewed in a test tube: sol-gel silica liners
idea: Po: 'the crucible is brewed in a test tube.' Extracted: for 150-200 mm pullers, whose crucibles are small, cast the melt-contact liner from synthetic silica made by sol-gel hydrolysis of silicon alkoxides (or flame hydrolysis of SiCl4) and sinter it onto a lower-grade quartz back wall, ending reliance on Spruce Pine natural quartz.
why: Breaks the >80% high-purity-quartz crucible chokepoint for 200 mm legacy-memory wafers on 1990s pullers; synthetic silica is purer than natural quartz.

title: Synthetic crucibles cast from polysilicon-plant SiCl4 waste
idea: Worsen: require Spruce Pine natural quartz for the inner layer of every Czochralski crucible. Flip: hydrolyze SiCl4, the main byproduct of Siemens polysilicon plants, into sol-gel silica and sinter it into the crucible's inner wall, keeping ordinary sand only for the outer structural shell.
why: High-purity quartz chokepoint (>80% Spruce Pine): turns a waste stream into crucible feedstock and takes HPQ demand for crucible inner layers toward zero.

title: Solyndra-proof loan guarantees for non-silicon memory fabs, indexed to DRAM prices
idea: Solyndra died in 2011 when the incumbent's input (polysilicon) price collapsed, not because its glass-tube technology failed. Structure CHIPS/DOE loans for glass-, foil- or SiC-substrate memory fabs with repayments indexed to a DRAM contract-price index (pausing below a floor) and tranches tied to tools re-taskable to displays or power devices.
why: The 4x 2025-26 price spike will reverse; indexed debt keeps chokepoint-free capacity alive through the down-cycle, roughly halving expected default loss and protecting U.S. manufacturability gains.

title: Card dealer slides boron-nitride sheets to store bits
idea: Persona: a card dealer sliding one card over another. In AB/BA-stacked bilayer hexagonal boron nitride, shifting one atomic sheet by one bond length flips the out-of-plane polarization (sliding ferroelectricity). Grow wafer-scale aligned bilayers by CVD on Cu(111) and use them as a FeFET gate or tunnel barrier.
why: Non-volatile switching with no bond breaking or ion migration, so in principle it does not fatigue. Uses only B and N.

title: Dental-resin chemistry for fluorine-free photoacid generators
idea: Dental composites are cured in human mouths with non-fluorinated photoinitiators because PFAS is unacceptable there. Synthesize non-fluorinated PAGs (sulfonium salts of camphorsulfonate or bulky sulfonated aromatic anions that limit acid diffusion) and benchmark sensitivity, LER and diffusion length on i-line and e-beam in a university fab.
why: The EU universal PFAS restriction threatens PFBS/PFOS-type PAGs in DRAM resists; a drop-in non-PFAS chemistry keeps the lithography supply legal and secure.

title: Spider-web electret nanofibre ULPA filters without PTFE
idea: Spider webs pull in charged particles electrostatically. Electrospin roll-to-roll cellulose-acetate or polylactide nanofibre mats carrying a permanent electret charge as fab ULPA media, replacing expanded-PTFE membranes.
why: Removes a PFAS material from cleanroom air handling and cuts filter pressure drop ~30-50%, lowering fan energy, the largest fab HVAC load.

title: Retired-server DIMMs reborn as CXL memory expanders
idea: Worsen: shred millions of working DDR4/DDR5 DIMMs whenever hyperscalers refresh servers every 4-5 years. Flip: run a take-back line that retests modules, maps weak rows and mounts the modules behind CXL controllers with stronger ECC and adaptive refresh as a far-memory tier.
why: Raises usable supply immediately with zero new wafers: each reused GB avoids nearly the full fab cost and could add several % to annual server DRAM supply.

title: Controlled-spalling wafer multiplication demo
idea: Within $1M/24 months: electroplate a stressed nickel layer on 300 mm prime wafers, start a crack to peel 20 um single-crystal films onto low-cost carriers, re-polish the parent and repeat ~20x; prove gate-oxide integrity and junction leakage on the spalled films.
why: Each CZ wafer (and its share of HPQ crucible and polysilicon) yields up to 20 device substrates; spalling is room-temperature and needs few tools, unlike ion-cut.

title: Postage stamp: half-inch minimal fab for oxide gain-cell tiles
idea: Stimulus 'postage stamp' -> a 10-person team runs a minimal-fab line (half-inch wafers, sealed local shuttles, no cleanroom) making zinc-tin-oxide gain-cell memory tiles below 400 C, bonded onto logic chiplets as near-memory.
why: Capital per line ~$10-30M versus $15B, no cleanroom HVAC and ~1/1000 the chemicals and water per tool; distributed U.S. manufacturability.

title: Silicon carbide access transistor: retention outlives the server
idea: Inverts 'the access transistor must be silicon': build 1T1C cells on 4H-SiC (3.26 eV gap, intrinsic carriers ~1e-9 cm^-3) so junction and subthreshold leakage drop by many orders of magnitude and a 5 fF node holds its level for years at 85 C; refresh circuits are deleted and lines run in idle US 150/200 mm SiC power fabs.
why: Zero refresh power (16-33% of idle power) and no refresh bandwidth loss; Si and C are abundant; adds US capacity from existing SiC fabs.

title: Gallium harvested from alumina-refinery Bayer liquor
idea: Periodic-table walk, Ga (31): install amidoxime ion-exchange columns on Bayer liquor (~100-200 ppm Ga) at U.S. and allied alumina refineries, turning a waste stream into tens of tonnes per year for oxide channels and GaN periphery power.
why: China holds ~98% of primary Ga under export controls; this route could cover U.S. semiconductor demand.

title: Po the fab drinks no water: supercritical CO2 clean and dry
idea: Po: 'the fab is built in a desert with no water.' Extracted: replace post-etch residue removal, rinse and spin-dry on most cleaning steps with supercritical CO2 plus alcohol and chelating co-solvents, recaptured and recompressed in a closed loop; the zero surface tension of scCO2 also stops tall capacitor pillars collapsing during drying.
why: Water intensity (large fabs draw millions of gallons per day; cleaning is the biggest use) cut by perhaps 30-50%, and the capillary-collapse limit on capacitor aspect ratio (fact 1) is lifted.

title: Liquid-nitrogen bathed memory pools nearly eliminate refresh
idea: Worsen: run DRAM hot (85-95 C) in air-cooled racks, so leakage forces 32-64 ms refresh. Flip: immerse pooled DRAM sleds in liquid nitrogen made from air on site. Junction leakage falls by orders of magnitude and retention stretches to minutes or hours, so refresh drops toward zero and VARY can come down.
why: Refresh energy (16-33% of idle power), row hammer margin and the voltage floor: memory power could fall ~3-5x, offsetting cryocooler cost, with no scarce coolant.

title: Existing U.S. solar ingot pullers make carrier wafers for bonded DRAM
idea: Scale shift across industries: bonded and stacked DRAM uses full prime CZ wafers as mechanical carriers and handles. Existing solar M12 ingot lines already pull ~300 mm-diameter ingots with lower-purity crucibles, so they can be sliced and polished into handle and monitor wafers.
why: Moves ~30-50% of DRAM's silicon wafer demand (carriers, handles, dummies) off prime CZ and HPQ crucibles onto existing capacity.

title: Substitute distillable organic solvent for water in final rinses
idea: Use a low-boiling non-PFAS solvent such as electronic-grade isopropanol or PGME as the rinse fluid in closed single-wafer tools, with on-tool vacuum distillation recovering >99% per cycle and a metal-scavenger resin bed.
why: Replacing water as the rinse carrier with a recirculated solvent cuts UPW in those steps >10x, and lower surface tension reduces drying collapse of tall structures.

title: Retrofit fab air-separation units to recover helium and neon
idea: Scale jump from atmosphere to fab: on-site ASUs at large existing fabs process ~4000 t/day of air for nitrogen. A non-condensable-gas column with a cryo-adsorber on the condenser vent captures neon (18 ppm, ~50 kg/day) and helium (5 ppm, ~20 L liquid-equivalent/day).
why: Partial self-sufficiency in two concentrated gases (helium from Qatar, neon for ArF/KrF lasers) through an ASU retrofit only.

title: Po capacitor made of white paint: rutile TiO2 on MoO2 electrodes
idea: Po: 'the capacitor dielectric is the white pigment in house paint.' Extracted: grow rutile-phase TiO2 (k ~80-110) at low temperature by templating it on a rutile MoO2 bottom electrode, which is lattice-matched like RuO2 but made from U.S.-mined molybdenum, and Al-dope it to suppress leakage, replacing ZrO2/HfO2 stacks and ruthenium.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1 needs k ~70): k ~90 gives ~1.5-2x Cs at the same aspect ratio, or lets the AR fall from ~70 to ~40; titanium and molybdenum are abundant and U.S.-sourced (Climax, CO), removing hafnium and platinum-group dependence.

title: Rutile TiO2 capacitor grown on lattice-matched MoO2 electrodes
idea: Worsen: make the capacitor dielectric depend on ever more Zr and Hf from zircon refining. Flip: grow rutile-phase TiO2 (k ~90-120) at low temperature by templating it on conductive rutile-structure MoO2 bottom electrodes, with a thin Al-doped TiO2 top layer to suppress leakage, using only abundant Ti, Mo and Al.
why: Capacitor charge wall (needs k ~70) and Hf/Zr dependence: ~1.5-2x Cs per pillar, or the same Cs at AR ~40 instead of 70, with no hafnium or zirconium.

title: Green-laser melt crystallizes each silicon tier using nine joules per wafer
idea: Melting a 20 nm Si film over a 300 mm wafer needs ~3 mg x ~2.8 MJ/kg = ~9 J, and a nanosecond pulse's ~100 nm thermal diffusion length keeps lower tiers cold. Deposit a-Si by PECVD and crystallize it with a green solid-state laser through grain-filter seed holes so each transistor sits in one grain; repeat for 32 tiers.
why: Crystalline-quality tiers at ~$15 per tier with no epi, no germanium and no neon excimer lasers; 32 tiers x relaxed cell = ~10x density at equal cost.

title: Cold-crucible levitation melting adapted from aerospace titanium skull melting
idea: Aerospace titanium is melted in water-cooled segmented copper cold crucibles, where induction fields push the melt off the wall and a thin frozen skull is the only contact. Adapt this to Czochralski growth: hold the silicon melt in an induction cold crucible with a solid-silicon skull and pull the crystal from the free surface.
why: Eliminates quartz crucibles entirely (Spruce Pine) and the oxygen they dissolve into the crystal, cutting per-ingot consumables. The challenge is getting a calm enough melt for dislocation-free growth.

title: Reject wafers reborn as passive interposers, bypassing ABF substrates
idea: Inverts 'HBM needs prime silicon interposers or organic ABF laminates': regrind test and yield-reject wafers into passive redistribution interposers with 2-3 copper layers patterned on mature i-line steppers, then hybrid-bond DRAM stacks and logic directly onto them.
why: Interposer silicon and single-supplier ABF film are CoWoS/HBM chokepoints; reclaimed wafers cost ~10% of prime and consume no new crucible quartz.

title: Pitch-octupling on old KrF scanners writes the DRAM array lattice
idea: Scale shift via spacer chemistry: the array is a perfectly periodic lattice. A 200 nm-pitch KrF line pattern in an existing 200 mm fab is divided by three spacer generations into 25 nm pitch, and the crossing hole lattice comes from two orthogonal passes. Periphery stays at native KrF resolution.
why: No EUV, no immersion and no new fab: unlocks idle 200 mm lines for 2-4 Gb DRAM. Accumulated CD variation is the risk.
